question: A 15-year-old adolescent presents to his pediatrician with progressive easy fatigability and exercises intolerance over the last several months. The patient was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery. He is up to date on all vaccines and is meeting all developmental milestones. There is no history of palpitation, dyspnea, or lower limb edema. On physical examination his vital signs are stable. On chest auscultation, a wide fixed split in the second heart sound is detected. A medium-pitched systolic ejection murmur is present which is best heard at the left middle and upper sternal border. A short mid-diastolic rumble is also audible over the lower left sternal border, which is best heard with the bell of the stethoscope. Which of the following findings is most likely to be present on this patient’s echocardiogram?

options.opb: Anterior movement of ventricular septum during systole
options.opc: Goose-neck deformity of left ventricular outflow tract
options.ope: Displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets inferiorly into right ventricle

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Wide fixed split in the second heart sound" -> "Atrial septal defect (ASD) likely present" -> "Increased right heart volume overload" -> "Right ventricular enlargement" -> "Decreased right ventricular end-diastolic dimension" -> 80% CHAIN: "Medium-pitched systolic ejection murmur at left middle and upper sternal border" -> "Pulmonary stenosis likely present" -> "Right ventricular hypertrophy" -> "Anterior movement of ventricular septum during systole" -> 75% CHAIN: "Short mid-diastolic rumble over lower left sternal border" -> "Mitral stenosis likely present" -> "Left atrial enlargement" -> "Goose-neck deformity of left ventricular outflow tract" -> 70% CHAIN: "Wide fixed split in the second heart sound" -> "Atrial septal defect (ASD) likely present" -> "Increased right heart volume overload" -> "Right ventricular dysfunction" -> "Increased left ventricular shortening fraction" -> 60% CHAIN: "Medium-pitched systolic ejection murmur at left middle and upper sternal border" -> "Pulmonary stenosis likely present" -> "Right ventricular enlargement" -> "Displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets inferiorly into right ventricle" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most likely finding on this patient's echocardiogram is displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets inferiorly into the right ventricle. This is supported by the chain linking pulmonary stenosis to right ventricular enlargement and the evidence path indicating displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets.
analysis: The patient's presentation with a wide fixed split in the second heart sound, a systolic ejection murmur, and a mid-diastolic rumble suggests a diagnosis of Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF). In TOF, displacement of the tricuspid valve leaflets inferiorly into the right ventricle is a characteristic finding due to the right ventricular enlargement. This displacement is known as overriding of the tricuspid valve. The other options are less likely in the context of TOF.
